executive_assessment.text: Chaco water constraints differ from eastern-region conditions; Indigenous community accounts around Irala Fernández identify storage and emergency-delivery gaps. Bañados adds a distinct urban flood-livelihood case.

Water-service competition and weak local grievance/institutional capacity are relevant mediators, but retrieved sources do not establish climate-caused violent conflict. Proposed community water and fire measures are not verified implementation.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated not stated reports: FAO says severe droughts have occurred about each decade since the 1960s; 2020–22 affected western Central Chaco, the Pilcomayo area, Irala Fernández and Mariscal Estigarribia, especially December–February.

Source dated not stated reports: FAO contrasts Central Chaco’s scarce, temporary, salty surface water and non-recharging salty groundwater with generally higher rainfall and more usable, recharging water resources in the east.

Source dated 2024 reports: In the Western Region (Chaco, Alto Paraguay, Boquerón, Presidente Hayes), the CCDR identifies high Indigenous concentrations and drought-related land degradation/water-access problems; riverbank bursts are associated with illness.
Source dated 2024 reports: A 2019–23 drought set the Paraguay River’s record-low at Asunción; in records since 1904, about 18% of observations would impede normal navigation near the city.
Source dated 2024 reports: Bañados near central Asunción is an informal settlement with rural migrants; floods average once in five years, causing relocation and job losses.

Source dated 2024-11 reports: The report names Chaco, Pilcomayo, Irala Fernández and Mariscal Estigarribia as drought-affected; poor rural/peri-urban, dispersed and Indigenous communities have limited WASH infrastructure.
Source dated 2020-11 reports: Chaco member accounts say water shortage and rainfall shifts alter crop calendars, reducing food crops, pasture and livestock feed.

FAPI's 2020 Chaco community accounts describe reliance on rainwater storage, scarce or saline water sources, insufficient storage through prolonged drought and water trucks not reaching Indigenous communities near Irala Fernández.
Source dated 2020-11 reports: FAPI says drought and heat raise fire threat; fires from adjacent lands/ranches damaged forests, crops and homes in Indigenous territories, including Itapúa and Caazapá.
Source dated 2020-11 reports: FAPI proposes local fire brigades, joint monitoring, agency complaint follow-up and territorial planning.

known_gaps.text: The reviewed accessible sources provide no verified source-stated pathway from named climate stress to organized violence or conflict escalation. UNICEF/DAPSAN reports generalized WASH service-use/access conflicts but supplies no case location, parties, timing or climate attribution.
Evidence is strongest for drought, WASH vulnerability, Indigenous Chaco accounts and some Asunción flooding; direct recent subnational conflict-security documentation remains a gap.
UN Human Security project material and GCF readiness material were not directly accessible; a MADES 2026 page returned 404. Search-index snippets were not used as findings.
The generalized WASH competition and service-access conflicts cannot support a specific climate→violence pathway without place, parties, chronology and mediator evidence.
FAPI plan proposals are distinguished from historical community accounts and are not represented as delivered or evaluated interventions.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
